title: Zodiac labels do not form a shared roster by clock position, fixed or rotating from sign to sign: calibrated positions from ZL3b, planted controls detected
statement: An extension of P-L4-010 with calibrated positions instead of index order. ZL3b records a clock position (<!hh:mm>) on each label line of the circular zodiac pages; I used those as each label's angle, so no rotation is fitted and no figure-to-word association is guessed. Pages: f70v1, f70v2, f71r, f71v, f72r1, f72r2, f72r3, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v. Rings are the label runs between circular text lines, counted from the outside (ring k on one page is compared with ring k on another); label lines before the first circular text (figures outside the circle on f73r/f73v) are excluded; words with uncertainty marks are dropped, and a label is all its remaining words joined. For every pair of pages and every shared ring, each label is compared with the label nearest its angle on the other page, if within 15 degrees: 1,303 comparisons. Observed: 0 exact label matches and 9 exact-or-one-edit matches (eva-basic glyphs). Null: labels shuffled within each ring of each page, positions kept, 999 permutations: mean 1.72 exact and 12.44 near; p = 1.0 (exact) and 0.89 (near), i.e. matches are if anything fewer than chance. With a 30-degree window (1,344 comparisons, 299 permutations): 0 and 9 observed, null means 1.78 and 12.71, p = 1.0 and 0.91. Power check: planting one shared word at 0 degrees and another at 180 degrees in the outer ring of every page gives 96 exact matches against a null mean of 11.2, p = 0.0033 (the minimum with 299 permutations). So a roster repeated at fixed clock positions, even for only two positions, would have been seen; none is. This agrees with the index-based result in P-L4-010 and is free of its rotation search. Rotating rosters: the same comparison, but for every pair of pages and ring the second page is rotated in 15-degree steps (24 offsets) in both directions and the offset with the most near matches is kept; the null applies the same maximisation to labels shuffled within rings (999 permutations). Observed: 17 exact and 78 near matches in 1,302 comparisons; null means 15.04 and 77.84; p = 0.196 (exact) and 0.543 (near). Power check for this version: planting the same two words at 0 and 180 degrees shifted by 30 degrees more on each successive page (a roster that rotates with the sign) gives 146 exact matches against a null mean of 85.5, p = 0.005 (the minimum with 199 permutations). So neither a fixed nor a rotating roster shared across signs is present at even two positions. Not tested: rosters in a different order on each page (no fixed sequence), which no position test can see.
check: script logic described above; inputs: data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt (pinned) label lines with clock comments on the twelve zodiac pages; seed 408; numbers as reported
